title.narrative: Integrated life-saving Nutrition, Child Protection and WASH response in conflict and flood-affected regions of Cameroon

description.narrative: The UNICEF Cameroon CERF project aims to address critical humanitarian needs in the conflict-affected regions of the Far North, North-West, and South-West, as well as to support continuous access to clean water and sanitation in flood-affected areas in the Far North.The child protection and nutrition activities will be implemented in the priority divisions as established by the Inter-Sector Working Group (ISWG) and thus contribute to a multisectoral approach beyond the UNICEF sectors in these intervention areas. The WASH activities inscribe themselves in the strategy developed for the climate envelope also be coordinated with the other recipient agencies.Child Protection: The child protection component targets 41,500 children and adolescents by distribution of essential child protection kits, comprehensive case management support for unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), provision of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and strengthening community-based protection mechanisms and promoting positive parenting practices.Nutrition: The nutrition component aims to support 77,489 beneficiaries, including. The primary objective is to deliver lifesaving interventions for children under five experiencing severe acute malnutrition (SAM). The main activities include early detection and referral of cases of SAM and moderate acute malnutrition (MAM), provision of nutritional commodities including therapeutic milk (F75 and F100), Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) and essential medicines for SAM treatment. community-based prevention activities and capacity building to service providers to ensure quality service provision. The WASH component focuses on climate response ensuring continuous access to clean water and sanitation in flood-affected areas in the Far North region to build local resilience of communities to climate related risks. The project includes activities designed to enhance the resilience of the affected communities. The project will construct flood-proof water supply systems and networks in schools and healthcare facilities in Logone and Chari. Additionally, flood-proof latrines will be installed to prevent contamination during floods, ensuring the functionality and accessibility of sanitation systems at all times. The dual-use solar-power systems will be introduced for water pumping and electricity provision in healthcare facilities and schools. Furthermore, water-saving technologies will extend water networks to improve access to clean water and reduce the risk of water-borne diseases. This is crucial given the overcrowded conditions in many areas, which heighten the risk of disease outbreaks.The climate envelope forms a crucial part of the UNICEF Cameroon CERF project, focusing on enhancing climate resilience in the flood-affected areas of the Far North region. The climate-specific objectives include constructing flood-proof water supply systems and latrines, introducing dual-use solar-power systems for water pumping and electricity provision, and implementing water-saving technologies. These activities aim to ensure continuous access to clean water and sanitation, even during and after floods, thereby reducing the risk of water-borne diseases and improving overall community health. The climate segment targets 40,000 people, including internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities, with a particular focus on vulnerable groups such as women, children, and persons with disabilities. By engaging local communities in the operation and maintenance of these systems and raising awareness about hygiene practices, the project fosters a sense of ownership and sustainability, ultimately contributing to the long-term resilience of these communities against climate-related risks.
